newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks closed mixed, seen guarded.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks closed mixed, seen guarded.

text.p: Argentine stocks closed mixed Friday and were seen hesitant ahead of the release of U.S. inflation data next week, dealers said.
"The market is at an impasse and is likely to stay rangebound until the U.S. Federal Reserve meets May 20," said Gabriel Armando at brokers Galicia Valores.
The blue-chip MerVal index shed 0.4 percent to 723.78, while the broad market closed up 0.3 percent.
Traders said U.S. price indicators due out Wednesday and Thursday could jolt the markets if they come in much stronger than expected.
"If the Fed finally decides to hike rates then the markets will retreat again as a natural reaction to a scenario of tighter credit," Armando said.
"But it will actually be a good buying opportunity, because it will probably be the last hike of the year and the markets will soon realize this and rise again," he added.
Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan said Thursday night the economy might slow down later this year and into 1997.
Floor volume picked up to 19.8 million pesos from a very weak 13.2 million Thursday, while over-the-counter turnover eased to 111.5 million pesos from 123.9 million Thursday.

Winning issues lagged losers 23 to 16 in the session and 23 issues closed unchanged. Worst main-tier performers were textile and footwear firm Alpargatas, which shed 2.2 percent, foods giant Molinos, off 1.9 percent, and carmakers Sevel and Ciadea, off 1.8 percent and 1.6 percent respectively.

Strongest MerVal risers were stocks listed abroad as ADRS. Banco Frances and Banco de Galicia rose 2.2 percent and 1.3 percent, respectively, encouraged by a drop in U.S. long bond yields which boosted their bond holdings. Telefonica and Telecom rose 1.2 percent and 1.0 percent each.
